summary: The final SQL/template wiring, named recording exclusion, valid-layout replay reset, and dedicated wraparound supervisor preserve their intended trust boundaries. However, the rounded-tie integration test still performs unconditional fixed-name DROP TABLE operations as postgres on the ordinary shared PG19 fixture, creating a blocking data-loss and cross-run interference risk. SC-1 also exposes its trust-authenticated synthetic cluster to the default Docker bridge, which permits evidence tampering by unrelated containers. Existing malformed-Ncols and terminal-control debts remain out of scope and are not represented as fixed. Scripted acceptance remains assigned to freeze-qa and manual SC-5 through SC-8 remain pending.

blocking_risks.finding: Rounded-tie integration test can delete unrelated shared-PG19 tables
blocking_risks.required_action: Remove fixed-name destructive probes from the shared fixture or move the complete test into an externally supervised, identity-checked disposable cluster before running the ordinary query suite or final QA.

findings.category: Privileged integration-test isolation / destructive database operation
findings.title: Rounded-tie integration test can delete unrelated shared-PG19 tables
findings.description: Test_StatAutovacuumScoresQuery_RoundedTieRawOrder uses the general PG19 connector and, without the dedicated marker or system-identity guard, executes DROP TABLE IF EXISTS on three fixed public-schema names before creating its probes and again during cleanup. NewTestConnectVersion maps this connection to the ordinary pgcenter_fixtures database as postgres on the standard PG19 endpoint. An operator or CI job running the documented AutovacuumScores/query test selection against a reused fixture therefore deletes any pre-existing relations with those names; concurrent runs can also drop each other's fixtures, including during cleanup after a failed CREATE. This is the same destructive shared-fixture class removed from Task 02, but Task 01's wraparound-only isolation does not cover this separate test. Attack vector: a local test/CI invocation against a shared or reused PG19 fixture causes irreversible data loss or cross-run integrity failures without any explicit destructive-test opt-in.
findings.evidence: Read-only Python source assertions returned rounded_tie_uses_general_pg19_connector=True, unconditional_fixed_name_drop_before_create=True, no_dedicated_marker_guard_in_test=True, and connector_targets_shared_pg19_endpoint=True. Git history shows the test file is newly added in this feature. The destructive test was deliberately not executed; no database object name or payload is sensitive evidence.
findings.recommendation: Do not issue anticipatory or fixed-name DROP statements on the shared fixture. Prefer running the rounded-tie fixture in the existing disposable, network-isolated, identity-checked supervisor with external destruction and a required test-level PASS. If it must remain in the ordinary suite, create a cryptographically unique per-run schema, safely quote its identifier, create only objects owned by that run, and clean up only that schema; add a regression guard proving an unmarked shared-suite run cannot perform persistent destructive SQL. Re-run the rounded-order mutation after the isolation change to retain behavioral evidence.

findings.title: SC-1 trust-authenticated PostgreSQL remains reachable from the default Docker bridge
findings.description: SC-1 starts its disposable PG19 container without a network restriction, configures PostgreSQL to listen on all addresses, and permits trust authentication for all IPv4 hosts. Loopback-only host port publishing does not remove access from other containers attached to the default bridge. An unrelated compromised container, or another local actor able to discover the ephemeral host port, can connect as postgres during recording, alter or drop the synthetic relations, reset statistics, or otherwise falsify the SC-1 evidence. The fresh no-secret workload limits confidentiality impact, but does not protect test integrity or isolate the destructive pg_stat_reset operation.
findings.evidence: Read-only Python checks over the frozen script returned acceptance_container_uses_default_bridge=True, acceptance_container_publishes_loopback=True, acceptance_postgres_listens_all=True, and acceptance_trusts_all_ipv4_hosts=True. This audit did not start the acceptance container or execute its reset workload.
findings.recommendation: Isolate SC-1 from the default bridge: either run PostgreSQL with --network none and execute the pgcenter client in that container's network namespace, as the wraparound supervisor does, or use a dedicated single-use network that unrelated containers cannot join while retaining only necessary loopback access. Keep the workload synthetic and verify external container destruction. Because this harness is frozen, route the correction through freeze-qa with a manifest refresh, clean base rerun, and renewed freeze review rather than editing the frozen artifact ad hoc.

findings.category: Untrusted deserialization / malformed archive bounds safety (existing debt [020])
findings.title: Malformed Ncols panic remains open but is not widened into a new feature blocker
findings.description: An untrusted archive can declare an excessive Ncols while keeping Cols and row widths internally consistent. PGresult.validate does not require Ncols == len(Cols), and the shared diff loop allocates and indexes using the declared width, so a second same-layout sample can panic report replay. The new slices.Equal check correctly handles valid adjacent layouts but does not validate dishonest dimensions. Attack vector: an operator replays a downloaded or replaced crafted tar archive and terminates pgcenter with an index-out-of-range panic. This is Task 04's previously reproduced debt [020], not a new in-scope regression; this feature neither fixes nor widens that malformed-shape class.
findings.evidence: Read-only source inspection confirms the missing Ncols/Cols equality check and the current-width diff loop. `git diff --exit-code <base>..<head> -- internal/stat/postgres.go internal/align/ top/stat.go` passed, proving those shared surfaces are unchanged. A read-only Python section comparison confirmed debt [020] is byte-identical across the feature range. Task 04's approved security report contains the earlier temporary-archive panic reproduction; it was not repeated or relabelled here.
findings.recommendation: Handle separately under debt [020]: reject negative or inconsistent Ncols/Nrows/Cols shapes, require Ncols == len(Cols), validate all consumer indices, and add malformed same-column-name replay tests requiring a clean error rather than a panic. Do not cite Decision 9 or SC-10 as a fix for this class.

findings.category: Terminal escape injection / server-controlled output (existing debt [029])
findings.title: New relation surface retains the documented unsanitised terminal-value debt
findings.description: The autovacuum_scores relation column concatenates server-derived schema and relation names, and the shared TUI printDataCell writes cell strings without removing terminal control sequences. A database principal able to create a hostile object name can therefore inject terminal controls when a DBA opens the new screen; pausing can prolong the crafted frame. Attack vector: a hostile or compromised database object name is rendered by an operator's terminal, potentially manipulating displayed content or terminal features. This is the explicitly extended pre-existing debt [029], not a new shared-renderer regression or blocker for this feature.
findings.evidence: Read-only data-flow inspection traces s.schemaname/s.relname through the PGresult value to fmt.Fprintf in printDataCell with no control-character sanitization. The feature-range diff leaves top/stat.go unchanged, and debt [029] explicitly records the new autovacuum_scores surface and the absence of a shared sanitizer fix.
findings.recommendation: Resolve in a separately scoped shared-output change: sanitize terminal control characters at the server/archive-to-terminal boundary while preserving intended SGR formatting and multibyte text, and add hostile relation-name tests for live and paused rendering. Continue to record the exposure until that shared fix lands; do not claim this feature closed it.
